inspiration: The logo is an inline SVG where the shapes reveal themselves with a one-shot CSS keyframe animation. Cheap way to make a title or splash reveal in our HUD with no video. Recreate with our own mark.
Behaviour trees are authored as XML with named node types, typed ports and reusable subtrees. Use the same split: creature brains as data files, code only for the leaf actions.
The node-mocking example runs a tree against stand-in nodes inside a test, to check flow without a game. Pattern for testing creature AI headless.
A SQLite logger records each tick of a tree for later replay (examples/ex03_sqlite_log.cpp). A scrubbable decision timeline for our debug overlay would follow this idea.

Ports are typed and remapped at the call site (file names t12 default ports, t13 access by reference, t19 polymorphic ports; not opened). One behaviour can then serve many creatures with different parameters.
A terminal manual-selector example (ex03_ncurses_manual_selector.cpp; name only, not opened) shows a hand-driven decision mode for debugging AI.
